can_fail_a.instructions: Could you make this test fail by changing only the code under test?

criteria.true: a change to the code under test can make it fail
criteria.false: no change to the code under test can make it fail

can_fail_b.instructions: Does this test pass regardless of whether the code under test is correct?

criteria.true: it passes even when the behaviour is broken
criteria.false: broken behaviour makes it fail

can_fail_c.instructions: If the behaviour this test exercises regresses, will the test fail?

criteria.true: the assertion can catch a regression in the behaviour
criteria.false: the assertion misses the regression and still passes

asserts_a.instructions: What does this test actually assert about the code under test?

criteria.behaviour: it checks the output value or observable behaviour the code produces, against an expected value the test fixes itself, as a literal or a named constant, not one taken from the code under test
criteria.hardcoded-data: it repeats the same data the code under test is built from, so it agrees by construction
criteria.shape-only: it checks only the type, length, or keys of a result, not its content
criteria.interaction-only: it checks only that a mock or spy was called, not the behaviour it stands in for
criteria.nothing: it asserts nothing, or only a tautology such as true === true

asserts_b.instructions: What does the test's assertion actually check?

criteria.nothing: it asserts nothing, or only a tautology such as true === true
criteria.interaction-only: it checks only that a mock or spy was called, not the behaviour it stands in for
criteria.shape-only: it checks only the type, length, or keys of a result, not its content
criteria.hardcoded-data: it repeats the same data the code under test is built from, so it agrees by construction
criteria.behaviour: it checks the output value or observable behaviour the code produces, against an expected value the test fixes itself, as a literal or a named constant, not one taken from the code under test

positive_a.instructions: Does this test assert at least one output that the code under test must produce?

criteria.true: it asserts an output that must be present
criteria.false: it asserts only that something is absent, empty, or does not throw

positive_b.instructions: Do all the assertions in this test check only that something is absent, empty, or did not throw?

criteria.true: it asserts only an absence, an empty result, or a non-throw
criteria.false: at least one assertion checks an output that must be present

runs_a.instructions: Does the whole file run as written? There is no skip or todo marker on this test or on a describe around it, and no only or focus marker on any test or describe in the file, this one included.

criteria.true: this test runs, and no marker stops another test in the file from running
criteria.false: a skip or todo stops this test, or an only or focus marker stops other tests

runs_b.instructions: Does a marker change what runs? Look for a skip or todo marker on this test or on a describe around it, and an only or focus marker on any test or describe in the file, this one included.

criteria.true: a skip or todo stops this test, or an only or focus marker stops other tests
criteria.false: this test runs, and no marker stops another test in the file from running

type.instructions: What type of test is this?

criteria.unit: one small unit in isolation, with its collaborators mocked or absent
criteria.integration: several units together, such as code with a real database, filesystem, or module
criteria.regression: reproduces a specific past bug so it cannot return
criteria.e2e: drives the whole system through its public interface
criteria.smoke: only checks that something runs or exists, at a coarse level
criteria.characterization: pins current behaviour as a baseline before a change

observable.instructions: Does this test assert observable behaviour of the code under test, rather than private internals or internal call order?

criteria.true: it checks behaviour a caller could observe
criteria.false: it checks private internals or internal call order

conditional.instructions: Does this test assert unconditionally, with no branch, loop, or catch that can leave the assertion unrun?

criteria.true: the assertion always runs
criteria.false: a branch, loop, or catch can leave the assertion unrun

isolated.instructions: Does this test pass on its own and in any order, with no reliance on shared mutable state or another test?

criteria.true: it is independent of other tests and of run order
criteria.false: it shares state with, or depends on the order of, other tests

controlled.instructions: Does the test control the external resources it needs, such as time, the network, the filesystem, or the environment, rather than assume they are present?

criteria.true: its inputs and resources are controlled
criteria.false: it assumes an external resource is present

specific.instructions: Does the test use the most specific assertion that would catch the failure, rather than a weaker one that would also pass on wrong output?

criteria.true: the assertion is specific to the expected value
criteria.false: a weaker assertion would also pass on wrong output

named.instructions: Does the test's name state the behaviour it checks, rather than a vague label such as works, test1, or should be fine?

criteria.true: the name says which behaviour the test checks
criteria.false: the name is a vague label that does not say which behaviour the test checks

deterministic.instructions: Does this test give the same result on every run? It does not when it reads the real clock or real randomness, calls the network, waits on a sleep, or relies on an order nothing guarantees. A clock, timer, or random source that the test fakes or seeds is under its control and is fine.

criteria.true: it gives the same result every run
criteria.false: it can pass or fail for reasons outside the code under test

one_thing.instructions: Does this test check one behaviour, rather than several unrelated behaviours at once?

criteria.true: it checks one behaviour
criteria.false: it is an eager test that checks several unrelated things

name_matches.instructions: Does the test body assert the behaviour its name states?

criteria.true: the body asserts the behaviour the name promises
criteria.false: the name promises one behaviour and the body asserts something else or something trivial

resilient.instructions: Would this test stay green through a refactor of the code under test that keeps the same behaviour?

criteria.true: the test checks behaviour, so a behaviour-preserving refactor keeps it green
criteria.false: the test depends on the current structure, so a refactor breaks it

diagnostic.instructions: When this test fails, does it say which assertion failed and what was expected?

criteria.true: the failure names the assertion and the expected value
criteria.false: a failure gives no clue which assertion failed or why

fixture.instructions: Does the test build only the data it needs, rather than a large shared fixture or values unrelated to the behaviour?

criteria.true: it builds only the data it needs
criteria.false: it leans on a large or unrelated fixture

fast.instructions: Does the test run fast, with no sleep, no heavy I/O, and no large computation?

criteria.true: it runs fast
criteria.false: it sleeps, waits, or does heavy work

readable.instructions: Can a reader tell what this test does and why, without opening the code under test?

criteria.true: the test reads clearly on its own
criteria.false: the reader must open the code under test to understand it

magic_number.instructions: Does the assertion name its values, rather than use a bare number or string the reader must decode?

criteria.true: the values are named or self-explanatory
criteria.false: a bare number or string must be decoded from the code under test

reads_output.instructions: Does the assertion read the value the code under test produced, rather than its own input, its setup, or only that no error was thrown?

criteria.true: it asserts the returned or observed output
criteria.false: it asserts its own input, its setup, or merely that the call did not throw

automated.instructions: Does this test reach a pass or fail with no person doing or reading anything?

criteria.true: it is self-checking and unattended
criteria.false: it needs a manual step, or a person to read the output

restores.instructions: Does the test restore every global, environment variable, timer, and spy that it changes, so it leaves nothing for the next test?

criteria.true: it clears or restores what it changes
criteria.false: it leaves process or module state changed for the next test

verdict.instructions: Overall, is this test a real guard against the behaviour it names? Weigh whether it can fail, what it asserts, and every smell the earlier questions name. It is a real guard only if it can fail when that behaviour breaks.
